text.title: Closed-Set Validation Failure Modes
text.summary: Six ways closed-set outputs fail, each with the observable symptom and the rule that prevents it.

failure.symptom: The system confidently returns a reference that matches every format check and resolves to nothing — a slug that reads plausibly, an ID with the right length and alphabet, a file path that does not exist.
failure.cause: The model authored the identifier from memory instead of selecting from a supplied set, and the only check was a regex on its shape.
failure.prevention: Supply the set, ask for a selection, then check membership. A regex proves an identifier is well-formed; membership proves it is real.

failure.symptom: The team believes hallucination is handled because there is code that drops bad values, and cannot state the rate when asked.
failure.cause: The drop writes a log line and continues; nothing counts it, so no test asserts and no user sees it.
failure.prevention: Increment a counter on the result. Live instance in faion-cli `internal/search/agent.go:270` (read 2026-08-03): correct drop, zero measurement.

failure.symptom: A judge model, an NLI dependency or a RAG-eval framework is added, costs real money per evaluation, and produces a number less accurate than a set intersection would have been.
failure.cause: The groundedness literature was applied without asking whether the output space was enumerable. It was.
failure.prevention: Compute the exact ratio first. Reach for entailment only for the fields that remain genuinely open after that.

failure.symptom: Correct answers are rejected as hallucinations; the rate looks alarming and the complaints are from users who were right.
failure.cause: The set was declared closed but was assembled incompletely, or came from a prior model turn rather than from a supplied artefact, so validation proved only self-consistency.
failure.prevention: Run all three conditions before writing the contract, and name the artefact the set comes from.

failure.symptom: A dashboard reads `grounding_rate: 1.00` while users are reporting wrong explanations next to correct links.
failure.cause: The metric covered the identifier field only, and nobody wrote down that the prose beside it was never checked.
failure.prevention: List the open fields in the contract and label the scope wherever the number is displayed.

failure.symptom: A release is blocked by a groundedness classifier, or a legal review discovers a non-commercial model inside a paid product's pipeline.
failure.cause: A scorer was adopted for its benchmark number without reading either its balanced accuracy or its licence.
failure.prevention: HHEM-2.1-Open (Apache 2.0) for triage; Bespoke-MiniCheck (CC BY-NC 4.0) never in a commercial product. At 64-77% balanced accuracy nothing here gates a release.
